passage: I'm Salma, and I've shared a bay with Jatin for a year. On Monday, Ramesh from logistics shipped the wrong spare parts to the Nagpur warehouse, his second slip in a month. Half the floor was muttering that Ramesh is careless. Jatin didn't join in. He walked over to Ramesh's desk with two cups of tea and asked, "Rough few weeks? What's been going on?" I couldn't hear everything, but Ramesh talked a lot and kept pointing at his screen. Later Jatin told me the new stock system shows two parts with nearly identical codes. "Could be the system, could be Ramesh rushing. Maybe both," he said. By Friday he'd asked IT to flag similar codes, and asked Ramesh to double-check orders before lunch. I don't know what Jatin really thought. But nobody muttered on Friday.

qa.a: Ramesh shipped the wrong spare parts to the Nagpur warehouse.

qa.a: Flagging similar codes deals with the system, and double-checking before lunch deals with any rushing, so both possible causes are covered.

qa.q: How might Ramesh have felt when Jatin came over with tea?

On the fourth floor of a Gurugram insurance office, Pankaj's claim files came back from audit with missing signatures for the third week running. "He's just sloppy," someone said at the coffee machine.
Hrithik, who sat opposite him, wasn't so sure. Pankaj had been leaving at exactly six every day lately, which he never used to, and answering calls in the stairwell.
So Hrithik asked, simply, over lunch: "The audit keeps flagging your files. Is something making the afternoons hard?"
Pankaj hesitated. "My father's been unwell. I do the files in a hurry before I leave to take him to appointments. I didn't want to make excuses."
"That's not an excuse. It's a reason," Hrithik said. "And the signatures are still a problem. Want to try doing the signature pass first thing in the morning?"
Pankaj nodded, looking relieved and a bit embarrassed at once.

"Vishal, got a minute?" Sarika pulled a chair to his desk. "The last three reports had the client's name spelled wrong."
Vishal rubbed his eyes. "I know. I'm sorry."
"I'm not here to scold. I'm curious. What's been going on?"
He hesitated. "We moved my mother in with us last month. She needs help at night. I've been sleeping maybe four hours."
"That sounds really hard."
"But also," he said, "I've never been great at proofreading. Even before."
"Okay. So maybe both things are true." Sarika nodded slowly. "For the tired part, could you do reports in the morning instead of late evening? And for the habit, want to try reading them aloud before sending? It works for me."
Vishal let out a long breath. "I thought you were going to call me careless."
"I nearly did," she admitted. "Then I wondered what I didn't know."

passage: Last spring Joseph started arriving late to our 9 a.m. stand-ups, three or four times a week. My first thought was the obvious one: he doesn't care any more. I actually drafted a message to our manager. But I've learned, the hard way, that I'm quick to decide things about people, so I deleted it and asked Joseph for tea instead. "Everything okay? You've been missing the mornings." He looked embarrassed. His building's water came only between eight and nine, and he was filling buckets for his elderly neighbours. "But honestly," he added, "I've always been bad with mornings." Both were true. We moved the stand-up to 9:30, and he set two alarms. He hasn't missed one since. The team calls me "Samir the detective" now. I'd rather be Samir who asks.

Hrithik missed the supplier call again today. Third time this month. My first thought, honestly, was: he's careless, and I'm tired of covering for him. I even started typing that to our manager. Then I stopped. Hrithik has never been like this before March. So what changed in March? I don't know. Maybe something at home, maybe the new commute, maybe he really is just slipping. Dolma

She went back to the account manager. "There's something hard happening for him, and our file system has a gap too. Both are true."

Dear Zubin,

I wanted to write rather than say this in the meeting.

Over the last two weeks, three of your reports have come in with missing sections. The team lead mentioned it, and I could see people starting to think you'd become careless.

I don't want to jump to that. You've been one of the most careful people on this team for two years. So I'm asking: is something going on? A heavier workload, something at home, the new software? Anything I can help with?

I also want to be honest: I've noticed you've stopped using the checklist we made last year. That might be part of it too.

Both can be true, a hard patch and a habit slipping. If it's either, let's sort it out together. If it's both, even better that we talk now.

Let's have tea tomorrow?

Sharmila
